chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"It is appropriate for the al-sarurah [unshaven pilgrim] to shave [his head], and if he has already performed Hajj, then if he wishes he may trim [shorten] and if he wishes he may shave [completely]."
He said, "And when he has let his hair grow long or trimmed it, then shaving is obligatory upon him and trimming is not sufficient for him."
And that which indicates that shaving is superior in all cases is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: The pilgrim who has not yet shaved or trimmed his head
key_terms.اَلتَّقْصِير: Trimming or shortening the hair (not full shave)
key_terms.لَبَّدَ: Letting hair grow long or thickening it

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between trimming and shaving the head for a pilgrim after Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic debate between permissibility and preference in the post-Hajj hair removal, establishing that while trimming is valid, complete shaving (halq) is superior and becomes obligatory if the hair reaches a length where it is considered 'letting it grow' (labbad). It reflects the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' detailed guidance on ritual purity and the symbolic completion of the pilgrimage state. The distinction highlights the importance of intention and physical state in fulfilling the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams.
